Terms of Use

Before you begin

This is a binding commercial agreement between your business and Mezzofy for use of the Merchant Portal at merchant.mezzofy.com. It incorporates the Commercial Terms agreed at onboarding and the Mezzofy policies (clause 1.4), and the English version prevails. You accept it by ticking “I Agree” at registration, or by creating, listing or redeeming any Pass.

§1

Parties and acceptance

1.1 This Agreement is between Mezzofy Holding Limited, a company incorporated in Hong Kong with company number 394841, and its affiliates that operate the Platform in the Merchant’s country (“Mezzofy”, “we”, “us”), and the business entity that registers for a Merchant Account (the “Merchant”, “you”).

1.2 You accept this Agreement by ticking the acceptance box at registration, by clicking “I Agree”, or by creating, listing or redeeming any Pass. Electronic acceptance has the same legal effect as a signed written agreement.

1.3 The individual accepting this Agreement confirms that they are authorised to bind the Merchant. If they are not, they accept personal responsibility for the Merchant’s obligations.

1.4 This Agreement incorporates by reference the Commercial Terms (pricing, fees and settlement schedule agreed at onboarding), the Published Pricing, the Support Policy, the Mezzofy Privacy Policy, the Acceptable Use Policy, the Pass Content Guidelines and any Country Addendum for the Merchant’s jurisdiction. If documents conflict, the order of priority is: (a) a signed Merchant Agreement or Country Addendum; (b) the Commercial Terms; (c) this Agreement; (d) the policies.

1.5 If you do not agree to this Agreement, do not register for or use the Portal.

§2

Definitions

In this Agreement:

  • “Platform” means Mezzofy’s coupon exchange infrastructure, including the Portal, the B2C Portal, the B2B Portal, the NFC Network, APIs, tokenisation and validation services, and settlement systems.
  • “Portal” means the Merchant Portal at merchant.mezzofy.com and any related merchant app or API.
  • “Pass” means any digital coupon, voucher, gift card, e-ticket, membership pass, stamp card or other redeemable entitlement created by the Merchant on the Platform, each identified by a unique Token.
  • “Token” means the unique, single-use digital identifier Mezzofy generates for each Pass to validate its authenticity and redemption status.
  • “Public Customer” means an individual who obtains a Pass through the B2C Portal, an NFC Node or a Distribution Partner.
  • “Enterprise Customer” means a business (such as a bank, telco, employer, HR or benefits platform, or loyalty operator) that buys or obtains Passes, usually in bulk, through the B2B Portal or API for distribution to its own users, employees or customers.
  • “Customer” means a Public Customer or an Enterprise Customer, and includes the end user who presents a Pass for redemption.
  • “Distribution Channels” means the B2C Portal, the B2B Portal, the NFC Network, Distribution Partners, AI and agentic commerce channels, and any other channel Mezzofy uses to offer Passes.
  • “Distribution Partner” means a third party Mezzofy authorises to market, distribute or resell Passes, including banks, telcos, malls, property operators, HR platforms, super-apps and AI platforms.
  • “NFC Network” means NFC tags, QR codes and similar touchpoints (each an “NFC Node”) deployed by Mezzofy or its channel partners in locations such as malls, offices and retail spaces.
  • “Face Value” means the price at which a Pass is offered to Customers, or the redemption value stated on the Pass where no price is charged.
  • “Gross Proceeds” means all amounts Mezzofy collects from Customers or Distribution Partners for a Merchant’s Passes.
  • “Net Settlement Amount” means Gross Proceeds (or the agreed Merchant settlement value) less Fees, Refunds, Chargebacks, taxes withheld and any other amounts Mezzofy may deduct under this Agreement.
  • “Fees” means the transaction, redemption, commission, distribution and service fees set out in the Commercial Terms.
  • “Redemption” means the validation of a Token at the Merchant’s point of sale or through the Platform, after which the Pass is marked used.
  • “Applicable Law” means all laws, regulations, regulatory guidance and industry rules that apply to a party, a Pass, a Customer or a transaction, in any jurisdiction.
  • “Zero Fee Pass”, “Charge Pass” and “Own-Channel Pass” have the meanings in clauses 3.6 and 8.2.
  • “Transacted Price” means the selling price the Merchant sets for a Charge Pass in the Pass Studio, less any discount the Merchant itself gives on that Pass, and excluding taxes collected on it. Discounts, subsidies or free distribution funded by Mezzofy, an Enterprise Customer or a Distribution Partner do not reduce the Transacted Price.
  • “Published Pricing” means the per-Pass usage rates for Own-Channel Passes published on Mezzofy’s website at mezzofy.com/for-merchants.html, as updated under clause 22.
  • “Support Policy” means Mezzofy’s support terms and service level agreement published at mezzofy.com/support.html, as updated from time to time.
§3

Mezzofy’s role

3.1 Mezzofy operates an exchange that connects Merchant Pass supply with Customers and Distribution Partners. The Merchant is the issuer of each Pass and is solely responsible for supplying the goods, services or benefits the Pass represents.

3.2 The Merchant appoints Mezzofy, on a non-exclusive basis, as its commercial agent to market, offer, sell and distribute Passes through the Distribution Channels, and as its limited payment collection agent to collect Gross Proceeds from Customers and Distribution Partners on the Merchant’s behalf. This payment collection appointment applies to Charge Passes only. Zero Fee Passes are a distinct pass type under which Mezzofy distributes the Pass on its own account and collects nothing on the Merchant’s behalf (clause 8.2). Own-Channel Passes are governed by clause 3.6.

3.3 A Customer’s payment to Mezzofy or to a Distribution Partner for a Pass discharges the Customer’s payment obligation for that Pass, whether or not Mezzofy has yet settled the amount to the Merchant. The Merchant must not seek payment for a Pass directly from any Customer or Distribution Partner.

3.4 Where the Commercial Terms specify a consignment model, the Merchant supplies Passes to Mezzofy on consignment for onward sale to Enterprise Customers or Distribution Partners. Title to the underlying benefit remains with the Merchant until Redemption, and Mezzofy settles only for Passes sold or redeemed as stated in the Commercial Terms.

3.5 Mezzofy is not a party to the supply of goods or services between the Merchant and a Customer, does not guarantee the Merchant’s performance, and is not a bank, stored value facility or escrow agent unless a Country Addendum states otherwise.

3.6 Pass Management System. The Merchant may also use the Portal as a pass management system to create, allocate, distribute and redeem Passes through its own channels and networks, such as its own stores, app, website, social media, CRM or loyalty programme (“Own-Channel Passes”). For Own-Channel Passes, Mezzofy acts only as a technology service provider. It is not the Merchant’s agent, does not offer or sell those Passes, and collects no payment from the Merchant’s customers. The Merchant is solely responsible for its own customers, pricing, payment collection, taxes, refunds and Pass Terms. Clauses 5, 7, 11 and 12 apply to Own-Channel Passes.

§4

Eligibility, verification and account

4.1 The Platform is for businesses only. The Merchant must be a legally registered entity (or a registered sole proprietor) in good standing in its country of operation, and must hold every licence and permit needed to supply the goods or services its Passes represent.

4.2 Before listing or settlement, the Merchant must complete Mezzofy’s Know-Your-Business (KYB) checks. These may include company registration documents, tax registration numbers, beneficial ownership details, identity documents of directors and authorised signatories, bank account verification and business licences. Mezzofy may repeat these checks at any time.

4.3 Mezzofy may decline, delay or restrict any registration or settlement where checks are incomplete, where information cannot be verified, or where Mezzofy considers there is a legal, regulatory, fraud or reputational risk.

4.4 The Merchant must keep all registration, outlet, contact, tax and bank details accurate and must update them in the Portal within 5 business days of any change. Mezzofy is not liable for misdirected or delayed settlement caused by inaccurate details.

4.5 Each business entity may hold one primary Merchant Account. Multiple outlets, brands or sub-users may be managed under that account. Additional accounts for affiliated entities require Mezzofy’s approval.

4.6 The Merchant is responsible for its credentials, for the access rights it grants to staff and sub-users, and for all activity under its account. It must enable any multi-factor authentication Mezzofy offers and must notify security@mezzofy.com within 24 hours of any suspected unauthorised access.

4.7 The Merchant may not sell, transfer, sub-license or share access to its account, except to its own authorised personnel.

§5

Creating and listing Passes

5.1 The Merchant may create Passes in the Portal and set their Face Value, quantity, quotas, validity period, participating outlets, redemption rules and terms and conditions (“Pass Terms”).

5.2 Pass Terms must be clear, complete, accurate and lawful in every market where the Pass is offered. They must state at minimum: what the Customer receives, any price or minimum spend, validity and expiry dates, participating outlets, blackout dates, booking requirements, exclusions, and whether the Pass is transferable or refundable.

5.3 The Merchant is solely responsible for all Pass content, including descriptions, images, prices, discounts, claims about origin, quality or dietary status (including halal, kosher, vegetarian or allergen claims), and any age or eligibility restrictions.

5.4 Mezzofy may review, edit for format, reject, pause or remove any Pass that breaches this Agreement, Applicable Law, the Pass Content Guidelines or a Distribution Partner’s content rules. Mezzofy has no obligation to review Passes, and its approval does not shift legal responsibility from the Merchant.

5.5 Once a Pass has been sold or issued, the Merchant may not reduce its benefit, shorten its validity or add restrictions for Customers who already hold it. Changes apply only to Passes issued after the change.

5.6 The Merchant must ensure it has capacity to honour every Pass it makes available. Inventory released to a channel is treated as committed for the stated validity period.

5.7 Passes are promotional entitlements to goods or services. They are not investment products, securities, currency, deposits or stored value, and must not be marketed as such. Where Applicable Law treats a Pass as a gift card, voucher or stored value product, the Merchant is responsible for the required disclosures, minimum validity periods and unclaimed property obligations, unless the Commercial Terms allocate these to Mezzofy.

5.8 Pass types and consent gate. When setting up each Pass in the Pass Studio, the Merchant must select its Pass type (Zero Fee Pass, Charge Pass or Own-Channel Pass) and enter the related setup inputs, such as Face Value, quantity, channels and validity. The Merchant consents to the charges and settlement terms for that Pass type under clause 8.2 when its authorised user clicks the “Publish” button in the Pass Studio, and no Pass can be published without that action. The click, together with the setup inputs recorded in the Pass Studio at that time, is the Merchant’s binding instruction and consent for that Pass. The Pass type of a published Pass cannot be changed; the Merchant must create a new Pass instead.

§6

Distribution channels

6.1 By listing a Pass, the Merchant authorises Mezzofy to offer it through any Distribution Channel, unless the Merchant restricts channels, markets or partners in the Portal. Current channels include:
  • B2C Portal — Mezzofy’s consumer-facing marketplace and apps, where Public Customers buy or claim Passes.
  • B2B Portal and API — where Enterprise Customers such as banks, telcos and HR platforms buy Passes in bulk or pull inventory into their own apps, rewards catalogues and employee benefit programmes.
  • NFC Network — NFC Nodes in malls, offices and other locations, where Public Customers tap to collect Passes.
  • Distribution Partners — third-party platforms, super-apps, loyalty programmes and resellers authorised by Mezzofy.
  • AI and agentic commerce channels — AI assistants and agents that discover, recommend and complete purchases of Passes through Mezzofy’s APIs and supported protocols.

6.2 Distribution Partners and Enterprise Customers may present Passes under their own branding, bundle them with their own rewards, offer them at a discount funded by themselves, or give them free to their users. The Merchant’s settlement for each Pass is determined by its Pass type under clause 8.2, regardless of the price a Distribution Partner charges its own users.

6.3 Mezzofy does not guarantee any volume of sales, Redemptions, placement or exposure on any channel, and may add, change or withdraw channels at any time.

6.4 The Merchant grants Mezzofy and its Distribution Partners the right to translate Pass content into the languages of each market. The Merchant remains responsible for the accuracy of its original content and should review translations made available in the Portal.

6.5 Unless the Commercial Terms say otherwise, the Merchant must not offer the same Pass on materially better terms through another channel in a way that misleads Customers who obtained it through Mezzofy. Nothing in this clause restricts the Merchant’s own pricing in its own stores.

§7

Redemption

7.1 The Merchant must honour and redeem every Pass it has issued, at every participating outlet, in accordance with the Pass Terms and without charging any amount not stated in those terms, for as long as the Pass is valid, has not expired, has not been voided and remains in active status on the Platform. The Platform’s validation record determines a Pass’s status (clause 7.3). The Merchant may not refuse, suspend or void an active Pass except through the Platform and as permitted by clause 7.6 or with Mezzofy’s written approval.

7.2 The Merchant must validate each Pass through the Platform before providing the benefit, using the Portal, the merchant app, an approved point-of-sale integration, or an NFC or QR verification method, and must follow Mezzofy’s authentication procedures.

7.3 Mezzofy’s Token validation record is the authoritative record of whether a Pass is valid, already redeemed or expired, absent manifest error. Mezzofy will not settle for Passes the Merchant accepts without validation, or that the Platform shows as already redeemed, expired or cancelled.

7.4 If the Platform is unavailable, the Merchant must follow the offline redemption procedure in the Portal help centre and record the Token for later validation. Mezzofy will settle offline Redemptions that are later validated as genuine and unused.

7.5 The Merchant must train its staff on redemption procedures and on recognising fraudulent Passes.

7.6 If the Merchant cannot honour a Pass (for example due to closure, sell-out or a change of business), it must notify Mezzofy immediately and, at Mezzofy’s choice, either provide an equivalent benefit acceptable to the Customer or fund a full refund to the Customer. For Zero Fee Passes, which are non-refundable, the Merchant must provide an equivalent benefit.

7.7 Unredeemed and expired Passes are treated as set out in the Commercial Terms, subject to Applicable Law on breakage, consumer refunds and unclaimed property.

§8

Fees, payments and settlement

8.1 Settlement is between the Merchant and Mezzofy only. Settlement applies to Charge Passes only; Zero Fee Passes and Own-Channel Passes involve no settlement. For Charge Passes, Customers, Enterprise Customers and Distribution Partners pay Mezzofy (or pay through Mezzofy’s systems), and Mezzofy settles to the Merchant. No Customer or Distribution Partner has any payment obligation to the Merchant, and the Merchant has no claim against them for settlement.

8.2 Pass types and charges. Listing Passes is free. The Pass type the Merchant selects and consents to at setup (clause 5.8) determines its charges and settlement:

  • Zero Fee Pass — Mezzofy charges the Merchant no Fees, and Mezzofy owes the Merchant no payment, for the sale, distribution or Redemption of the Pass. Customers may receive the Pass free of charge, or Mezzofy, Enterprise Customers or Distribution Partners may charge for it; any amount they collect is not payable to the Merchant. The Merchant must honour every Zero Fee Pass at its own cost. Zero Fee Passes are non-refundable (clause 10.6).
  • Charge Pass — For each Charge Pass that is both sold and redeemed, Mezzofy pays the Merchant 90% of the Transacted Price and retains 10% as its Fee. No settlement is due for Charge Passes that are refunded, charged back, or sold but not redeemed (subject to clause 7.7).
  • Own-Channel Pass — Mezzofy charges per-Pass usage fees for allocation, distribution and redemption at the rates in the Published Pricing at the time of use. Mezzofy collects no proceeds and makes no settlement for Own-Channel Passes.

8.3 Mezzofy collects payments through licensed payment service providers (currently including Stripe) and bank transfer. The Merchant agrees to complete any verification those providers require and acknowledges that payouts may be subject to their processing times and rules.

8.4 Monthly Charge Pass settlement. Mezzofy will pay the Net Settlement Amount for all Charge Passes redeemed in a calendar month to the Merchant’s verified bank account by the last day of the following month. Amounts below the minimum payout of USD 500 (or its equivalent in the settlement currency) may be carried forward to the next month.

8.5 Settlement is made in the currency in the Commercial Terms. Settlement to Merchants in Indonesia is made in Indonesian Rupiah where Indonesian law requires. Where currency conversion is needed, Mezzofy or its payment providers apply their prevailing exchange rate at the time of conversion, and bank, intermediary and conversion charges are borne by the Merchant unless agreed otherwise.

8.6 Mezzofy will make a settlement statement available in the Portal for each cycle. The Merchant must raise any dispute about a statement in writing within 30 days of its availability. After that period, the statement is final, except for fraud or manifest error.

8.7 Mezzofy may deduct from any amount owed to the Merchant: Fees; Refunds and Chargebacks; taxes Mezzofy must withhold; amounts paid for Passes the Merchant failed to honour; fines or charges imposed by payment providers or regulators due to the Merchant’s conduct; and any other amount the Merchant owes Mezzofy. If amounts owed exceed settlement due, the Merchant must pay the difference within 14 days of invoice.

8.8 Mezzofy may hold a reserve or delay settlement where it reasonably believes there is elevated risk of Refunds, Chargebacks, fraud, non-performance, insolvency or regulatory action, or where the Merchant has received a termination notice. Mezzofy will tell the Merchant the reason and expected duration where lawful, and will release reserves once the risk has passed.

8.9 If Mezzofy pays the Merchant an amount in error, the Merchant must repay it on request, and Mezzofy may recover it from future settlements.

8.10 Gross Proceeds held by Mezzofy before settlement do not earn interest for the Merchant.

8.11 Own-Channel usage fees. Usage fees for Own-Channel Passes are calculated from the allocation, distribution and redemption counts recorded on the Platform, invoiced monthly in arrears, and payable within 14 days of invoice. Mezzofy may set off unpaid usage fees against any Charge Pass settlement.

§9

Taxes

9.1 Fees are exclusive of GST, VAT, SST, sales tax and similar taxes, which will be added where applicable. Mezzofy will issue tax invoices for its Fees where required.

9.2 The Merchant is solely responsible for determining, collecting, reporting and paying all taxes on the supply of goods and services represented by its Passes, including output tax on redemption or sale, and income tax on its proceeds.

9.3 Where Applicable Law requires Mezzofy to withhold tax from payments to the Merchant, Mezzofy will deduct it and provide evidence of payment where available. Where Mezzofy is required to collect and remit tax on the Merchant’s behalf (for example as a marketplace operator), the Merchant authorises Mezzofy to do so.

9.4 The Merchant must provide valid tax registration numbers and any tax residency or treaty forms Mezzofy reasonably requests, and indemnifies Mezzofy against taxes, interest and penalties arising from incorrect information.

§10

Refunds, cancellations and chargebacks

10.1 Customer refund rights are set by the Pass Terms, Mezzofy’s Customer terms and Applicable Law, including mandatory consumer protection rights that cannot be excluded.

10.2 Mezzofy may refund a Customer, and recover the refunded amount (including Fees and payment costs) from the Merchant, where: the Merchant refused or failed to honour a valid Pass; the Pass was materially misdescribed; the Merchant closed, stopped trading or changed its offer; a Customer is entitled to a refund under Applicable Law; or a payment is reversed as a Chargeback attributable to the Merchant.

10.3 Where a refund is not attributable to the Merchant (for example a duplicate payment or a Platform error), Mezzofy bears the cost.

10.4 The Merchant must cooperate with Mezzofy in responding to Customer complaints and Chargebacks, including providing redemption records, receipts and other evidence within 3 business days of request.

10.5 Excessive Refund or Chargeback rates, as defined in the Commercial Terms or by Mezzofy’s payment providers, may lead to reserves, suspension or termination.

10.6 Zero Fee Passes are non-refundable. To the extent permitted by law, no refund is payable to any Customer for a Zero Fee Pass, clause 10.2 does not apply to Zero Fee Passes, and Mezzofy will not recover any refund amount from the Merchant for them. The Merchant’s obligation to honour Zero Fee Passes under clause 7.1 is unaffected.

§11

Fraud prevention and platform security

11.1 Mezzofy issues a unique Token for each Pass and applies validation, velocity and anomaly controls to prevent duplication, counterfeiting and abuse. The Merchant must not bypass, disable, reverse-engineer or interfere with these controls.

11.2 Mezzofy may block, cancel or reissue any Token, and may pause a Pass or the Merchant Account, where it detects or reasonably suspects fraud, abuse, bot activity, collusion or a security incident, whether by a Customer, the Merchant’s staff or a third party.

11.3 The Merchant is liable for losses arising from fraud or misuse by its own staff, contractors or systems, including Passes redeemed without valid Tokens or fake Redemptions recorded through its account.

11.4 Mezzofy is not liable for losses from fraud the Merchant could have prevented by following the redemption procedures in clause 7.

11.5 NFC tags, QR codes and devices supplied by Mezzofy or its channel partners remain their property. The Merchant must not tamper with, copy, relocate or reprogramme them, and must report damaged or suspicious tags promptly.

§12

Data protection and privacy

12.1 Each party will comply with data protection laws that apply to it, which may include the Singapore PDPA, the Malaysian PDPA, Indonesia’s Personal Data Protection Law (Law No. 27 of 2022), Hong Kong’s PDPO, China’s PIPL, the UAE PDPL, Saudi Arabia’s PDPL, India’s DPDP Act, the EU and UK GDPR, and US state privacy laws such as the CCPA.

12.2 Mezzofy is an independent controller of Customer personal data it collects through the Platform, as described in its Privacy Policy. The Merchant receives Customer personal data only as needed to validate Passes, fulfil the benefit and handle Customer service (“Permitted Purposes”).

12.3 The Merchant must not use Customer personal data received through the Platform for its own marketing, profiling, resale or any purpose other than the Permitted Purposes, unless the Customer has given separate, verifiable consent directly to the Merchant. Data from Enterprise Customers’ users may be subject to additional restrictions communicated by Mezzofy.

12.4 The Merchant must protect Customer personal data with appropriate technical and organisational measures, limit access to staff who need it, and delete it when no longer needed for the Permitted Purposes.

12.5 Mezzofy protects data on the Platform using industry-standard security measures, including encryption of personal data in transit and at rest. Mezzofy may store and process data in, and transfer it to, countries other than the Merchant’s or Customer’s country, with safeguards required by Applicable Law.

12.6 The Merchant must notify Mezzofy at security@mezzofy.com within 24 hours of becoming aware of any actual or suspected breach affecting Customer data or Platform credentials, and must cooperate with investigation, regulator notifications and Customer communications.

12.7 Mezzofy may use transaction and redemption data, including Merchant data, to operate and secure the Platform, prevent fraud, meet legal obligations, and produce aggregated or de-identified analytics and market insights. Aggregated data that does not identify the Merchant or any individual may be used and shared by Mezzofy, including in intelligence products for other parties.

12.8 Where the Merchant processes personal data on Mezzofy’s behalf, or vice versa, the parties will sign Mezzofy’s Data Processing Addendum.

§13

Merchant obligations and compliance

13.1 The Merchant must:

  • (a) comply with Applicable Law in every market where its Passes are offered or redeemed, including consumer protection, fair trading, advertising, pricing, product safety, food hygiene, licensing and promotional laws;
  • (b) maintain all business licences, permits and certifications, including halal or other certifications it claims or is legally required to hold (such as halal certification under Indonesia’s Halal Product Assurance Law), and provide copies on request;
  • (c) supply goods and services of the quality, quantity and description stated in the Pass Terms;
  • (d) provide prompt and courteous customer service, and respond to Customer complaints forwarded by Mezzofy within 2 business days;
  • (e) keep accurate records of all Redemptions for at least 5 years, or longer if Applicable Law requires, and make them available to Mezzofy on request;
  • (f) restrict Passes for age-restricted or regulated goods (such as alcohol) to eligible Customers and verify age at redemption; and
  • (g) treat Customers who use Passes no less favourably than other customers, including on service, portion size and availability.

13.2 Sanctions and export controls. The Merchant represents that neither it nor its owners, directors or controllers are subject to sanctions administered by the United Nations, the United States, the European Union, the United Kingdom or any country where the Merchant operates, and it will not use the Platform for any transaction involving a sanctioned person or territory.

13.3 Anti-money laundering. The Merchant must not use Passes or the Platform to launder money, finance terrorism, disguise the source of funds or evade capital controls, and must provide information Mezzofy reasonably requests to meet its own AML obligations.

13.4 Anti-bribery. The Merchant must comply with applicable anti-bribery and anti-corruption laws, including the UK Bribery Act and the US FCPA where applicable, and must not offer Passes or anything of value to any official, Enterprise Customer employee or Distribution Partner employee to obtain improper advantage.

13.5 Islamic finance and local requirements. Where a Country Addendum or Distribution Partner requires Sharia-compliant structures or other local requirements, the Merchant will comply with the additional terms notified to it for that market.

§14

Prohibited activities

The Merchant must not:

  • (a) create fake, duplicate or self-generated Redemptions, or redeem Passes without providing the benefit;
  • (b) buy its own Passes, or arrange for others to do so, to inflate sales or obtain settlement or incentives;
  • (c) misrepresent its business, products, prices, discounts or Pass Terms, or use bait-and-switch practices;
  • (d) list Passes for illegal, counterfeit, stolen or restricted goods or services, adult content, gambling, weapons, tobacco or vaping products, cryptocurrency or financial products, or any category in the Acceptable Use Policy;
  • (e) generate excessive Chargebacks or Refunds through its own conduct;
  • (f) attempt unauthorised access to the Platform, other merchants’ accounts or Customer data, or scrape, probe or overload the Platform;
  • (g) reverse-engineer, copy or build a competing service using the Platform, its APIs or its data;
  • (h) contact Customers obtained through the Platform to divert sales away from it, or sell Passes received through Mezzofy outside the Platform;
  • (i) infringe the intellectual property, privacy or other rights of Mezzofy or any third party;
  • (j) charge Customers surcharges or require purchases not stated in the Pass Terms; or
  • (k) resell, transfer or share Portal access with unauthorised parties.
§15

Intellectual property

15.1 Mezzofy and its licensors own all rights in the Platform, including software, APIs, Token and validation technology, designs, data models, trademarks and documentation. The Merchant receives a limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable, revocable licence to use the Portal during the term solely to perform this Agreement.

15.2 The Merchant grants Mezzofy, its affiliates and its Distribution Partners a worldwide, non-exclusive, royalty-free licence during the term (and afterwards for Passes already issued) to use, reproduce, adapt, translate, display and distribute the Merchant’s names, logos, trademarks, images and Pass content, solely to operate, market and distribute Passes and to promote the Platform.

15.3 The Merchant warrants that it owns or is licensed to use all content it uploads, and that Mezzofy’s use under clause 15.2 will not infringe any third-party right.

15.4 Mezzofy may identify the Merchant as a Platform participant in marketing materials, unless the Merchant opts out in writing.

15.5 Feedback and suggestions the Merchant provides about the Platform may be used by Mezzofy freely and without obligation.

§16

Confidentiality

16.1 Each party must keep confidential the non-public information of the other it receives under this Agreement, including the Commercial Terms, Fees, settlement data, technical information and business plans, and use it only to perform this Agreement.

16.2 This obligation does not apply to information that is public through no fault of the recipient, already known to it, independently developed, or required to be disclosed by law or a regulator (with prompt notice to the other party where lawful).

16.3 Confidentiality obligations continue for 3 years after termination, and indefinitely for trade secrets and personal data.

§17

Representations and warranties

17.1 Each party represents that it is duly organised, has authority to enter this Agreement, and that doing so does not breach any other agreement binding on it.

17.2 The Merchant further represents and warrants that all information it provides is true and complete, that it can and will honour every Pass it issues, and that its Passes and business comply with Applicable Law.

§18

Indemnity

§20

Term, suspension and termination

20.1 This Agreement starts when the Merchant accepts it and continues until terminated.

20.2 Either party may terminate this Agreement for convenience on 30 days’ written notice, given through the Portal or by email.

20.3 Mezzofy may suspend the Merchant Account, specific Passes, channels or settlement immediately, or terminate this Agreement immediately by notice, if: the Merchant materially breaches this Agreement; Mezzofy reasonably suspects fraud, sanctions exposure or illegal activity; the Merchant becomes insolvent, enters administration or ceases trading; a payment provider, Distribution Partner or regulator requires it; or the Merchant’s Refund, Chargeback or complaint rates exceed acceptable levels. Mezzofy will give reasons where lawful.

20.4 Passes already issued must be honoured. Termination does not affect Passes sold or issued before the termination date. The Merchant must continue to honour them under clause 7.1 for as long as they remain valid, unexpired, not voided and active, unless Mezzofy agrees to cancel and refund them, in which case the Merchant must fund those refunds.

20.5 On termination, Mezzofy will remove the Merchant’s unsold Passes from all Distribution Channels within a reasonable period, settle Net Settlement Amounts properly due (less any reserve under clause 8.8, held for up to 180 days or until the last issued Pass expires, whichever is later), and invoice any amounts the Merchant owes.

20.6 The Merchant may export its data from the Portal for 30 days after termination. After that, Mezzofy may delete or anonymise Merchant data, except data it must keep under Applicable Law or for fraud prevention, accounting or dispute purposes.

20.7 Clauses on payment and settlement, taxes, Refunds, data protection, intellectual property, confidentiality, indemnity, limitation of liability, governing law and any other provisions intended to survive will survive termination.

§21

Governing law and dispute resolution

21.1 This Agreement is governed by the laws of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, without regard to conflict-of-law rules, unless a Country Addendum specifies otherwise for the Merchant’s jurisdiction.

21.2 The parties will first try to resolve any dispute through good-faith negotiation between senior representatives for 30 days after written notice of the dispute.

21.3 Any dispute not resolved by negotiation, including any question about the existence, validity or termination of this Agreement, will be finally resolved by arbitration administered by the Hong Kong International Arbitration Centre (HKIAC) under the HKIAC Administered Arbitration Rules in force at the time. The seat of arbitration is Hong Kong, the tribunal will consist of one arbitrator, and proceedings will be in English. The award is final and binding.

21.4 Either party may seek urgent injunctive or interim relief from any competent court to protect its intellectual property, confidential information or Platform security, or to recover undisputed sums.

21.5 To the extent permitted by law, claims must be brought individually and not as a plaintiff or class member in any class, collective or representative proceeding.

21.6 Mandatory rights of the Merchant under the law of its own country that cannot be excluded by contract are not affected by this clause.
